title: Mahremiyetin fiyatı
text: Debates about privacy are conducted almost entirely in the language of individual choice, and that framing is the source of most of the confusion. A person is offered a service, told what will be collected, and clicks to accept; whatever follows is presented as the consequence of a free decision. The account would be more persuasive if the decision were genuinely individual. When a substantial proportion of a population shares its behavior, the inferences that become possible apply to everybody, including those who refused. A model trained on the movements of a million willing participants can predict the movements of the abstainer, because human behavior is correlated and the abstainer is not an exception to the patterns the model has learned. This is why the analogy with property fails. If I sell my furniture, your furniture is unaffected; if I sell my data, I have also sold a statistical portrait of you. Regulators have begun, slowly, to recognize the problem, but the remedies remain individual: a right to see what is held, a right to delete it, a right to object. Each of these is worth having and none addresses the structure. A more honest approach would treat certain inferences as impermissible regardless of consent, in the way that some contracts are void even when both parties sign willingly. That move is resisted because it removes the comfortable fiction that the person who clicked has authorized everything that follows, and because it requires somebody to decide which inferences are unacceptable, which is a political question rather than a technical one, and therefore the kind of question modern institutions are least equipped to answer. There is a precedent, and it is instructive. Employment law in most countries does not permit a worker to consent to unlimited hours, on the reasoning that the consent is extracted under conditions the worker did not choose and that the harm falls partly on others. Nobody regards this as an insult to the worker's judgment. Applying the same reasoning to data would not be a novel move; it would be the ordinary recognition that consent does its moral work only when the person consenting is in a position to refuse.

questions.q: What does the author say is the source of the confusion?
questions.note: İlk cümle.

questions.q: Why is the decision not genuinely individual?
options: Inferences apply to those who refused too
questions.note: Model, katılmayanın hareketlerini de tahmin edebiliyor.

questions.q: Why does the property analogy fail?
options: Selling your data sells a portrait of others
questions.note: "If I sell my data, I have also sold a statistical portrait of you."

questions.q: What do current remedies have in common?
questions.note: Görme, silme, itiraz hakkı — hepsi bireysel.

questions.q: What does the author propose instead?
options: Treating some inferences as impermissible regardless of consent
questions.note: Rıza olsa bile bazı çıkarımlar yasaklanmalı.

questions.q: Why is that move resisted?
options: It requires a political decision institutions avoid
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Mimarlıkta dürüstlük
text: Among the principles that architects inherited from the modern movement, none has proved more durable or more slippery than the demand for honesty. A building should express its structure; materials should appear as what they are; ornament that conceals construction is a kind of lie. Stated in that form the principle sounds almost self-evident, and for several decades it produced work of remarkable clarity. Its difficulties emerge as soon as one asks what a building is being honest about. A steel frame wrapped in fireproofing and then clad in steel panels is, in the literal sense, concealing its structure behind a representation of that structure, and some of the most admired buildings of the period do exactly this. The panels are not structural; they are a sign meaning structure. Once that is noticed, honesty turns out to be a style rather than an absence of style, with its own conventions, its own permitted materials and its own characteristic dishonesty, which is the pretense that a set of aesthetic preferences is a moral requirement. The interesting question is why the vocabulary of virtue attached itself to architecture so firmly, when we do not usually ask a chair to be truthful. One plausible answer is that buildings are imposed. Nobody is obliged to read a novel they dislike, but the inhabitants of a street must look at whatever is built there for the rest of their lives, and a profession that exercises that kind of power without a license from the people affected will reach, almost inevitably, for a justification framed in ethical terms. None of this is an argument for ornament, and the modern movement produced buildings that remain among the best of the century. It is an argument for describing taste as taste. A profession that says it prefers exposed concrete is making a claim anybody can disagree with; a profession that says exposed concrete is honest has placed its preference beyond argument, and has done so using a word that belongs to a different subject entirely.

questions.q: What does the principle of honesty demand?
options: That a building express its structure
questions.note: İkinci cümle.

questions.q: What problem does the clad steel frame reveal?
options: The panels are a sign meaning structure, not structure
questions.note: "The panels are not structural; they are a sign meaning structure."

questions.q: What does honesty turn out to be?
options: A style with its own conventions
questions.note: "Honesty turns out to be a style rather than an absence of style."

questions.q: What is its characteristic dishonesty?
options: Presenting taste as a moral requirement
questions.note: Estetik tercihin ahlaki zorunluluk gibi sunulması.

questions.q: Why do we not ask a chair to be truthful?
options: A chair is not imposed on everyone
questions.note: Binalar dayatılır, sandalyeler dayatılmaz.

options: Architects exercise power without permission from those affected
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Belgeselin kurgusu
text: Audiences approach documentary with an expectation they would never bring to a novel: that what they are watching is, in some straightforward sense, what happened. The expectation survives despite everyone knowing that a camera must be placed somewhere, that a hundred hours are reduced to ninety minutes, and that music is added afterwards to tell the viewer how to feel. Each of these is a fictional operation in the technical sense — a shaping of material according to a purpose — and none of them is dishonest, because no alternative exists. A film that refused to choose would be unwatchable and would still have chosen, by leaving the camera running in one place rather than another. The genuine ethical questions lie elsewhere, and are rarely the ones audiences ask about. They concern the relationship between the filmmaker and the person filmed, who has usually agreed to participate without any realistic idea of how they will appear when their words are placed beside somebody else's. A subject can consent to being recorded; they cannot meaningfully consent to an edit that does not yet exist. Some directors have responded by showing participants the finished film and offering a veto, a practice that produces obvious problems of its own, since the most revealing material is precisely what a subject is most likely to remove. Others argue that the obligation runs to the audience instead, and that softening a portrait to protect its subject is a betrayal of the form. The disagreement has no settled answer, which is perhaps why the more thoughtful documentaries have started to make the negotiation visible, leaving in the moments where the person on screen asks what exactly this is going to be used for. The device is not a solution and is sometimes merely another effect, since a filmmaker who shows you the negotiation has also chosen which negotiation to show. What it does accomplish is to remove the pretense of absence. A viewer who has watched somebody hesitate before answering is unlikely to forget, ten minutes later, that a person with a camera was standing there.

questions.q: What expectation do audiences bring?
options: That what they see is what happened
questions.note: İlk cümle.

questions.q: Why are the shaping operations not dishonest?
questions.note: "None of them is dishonest, because no alternative exists."

questions.q: Where do the genuine ethical questions lie?
options: In the length of the film
In the relationship with the person filmed
questions.note: "They concern the relationship between the filmmaker and the person filmed."

questions.q: What can a subject not meaningfully consent to?
options: An edit that does not yet exist
questions.note: "They cannot meaningfully consent to an edit that does not yet exist."

questions.q: What is the problem with offering a veto?
options: Subjects remove the most revealing material
questions.note: En açıklayıcı malzeme tam da kaldırılmak istenendir.

questions.q: How have thoughtful documentaries responded?
options: By making the negotiation visible on screen
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Kıtlığın icadı
text: Economics defines itself as the study of scarcity, which sounds like a description of the physical world and is in fact a description of a relationship. A resource is scarce relative to the demands placed on it, and those demands are not fixed facts but the product of arrangements that could be otherwise. Water in a dry region is scarce in a way that no institution invented; water in a wet region where agriculture has been organized around a thirsty crop is scarce in a quite different sense, and confusing the two has consequences. The first situation calls for allocation; the second calls for asking who decided on the crop. This distinction is routinely lost because the vocabulary of scarcity carries an implication of natural limit, which is politically convenient for whoever benefits from the current arrangement. Housing offers the clearest contemporary example. In several cities where residential space is described as scarce, the quantity of built space per person has risen steadily for decades. What changed was not the supply of rooms but the rules governing who may occupy them and at what price, together with the conversion of housing from a place to live into an instrument for storing wealth. Describing the outcome as scarcity is not false, since people genuinely cannot find somewhere to live, but it is incomplete in a way that points policy in a particular direction: towards building more, which is slow and profitable, and away from asking what the existing stock is being used for, which is fast and unpopular. Economists are not responsible for this elision, and many have spent careers pointing it out, but the word does most of the work before the argument begins. This is worth stating plainly because the alternative framings are available and unused. One could describe the same situation as a distribution problem, or as a question of what the built environment is for, and each of those phrasings would recruit a different set of experts and permit a different set of solutions. Vocabulary is not a neutral wrapper around policy; it is the first policy decision, taken before anybody notices that a decision has been made.

questions.q: What is scarcity really a description of?
questions.note: İlk cümle.

questions.q: What does the second kind of scarcity call for?
options: Asking who decided on the crop
questions.note: "The second calls for asking who decided on the crop."

questions.q: Why is the distinction routinely lost?
options: The word implies a natural limit
questions.note: Kıtlık sözcüğü doğal sınır çağrışımı taşıyor.

questions.q: What has happened to built space per person in those cities?
questions.note: "Has risen steadily for decades."

questions.q: What does the scarcity framing point policy towards?
questions.note: Yavaş ve kârlı olan yöne: daha çok inşaat.

questions.q: What does the author say about economists?
options: They are not responsible for the elision
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Unutmanın işlevi
text: Forgetting is generally treated as a defect, a failure of a system that would work better if it retained everything. The assumption survives because the costs of forgetting are visible and the costs of remembering are not. A person who cannot find a name is obviously inconvenienced; a person who cannot stop retrieving irrelevant detail appears, at first, merely well informed. The clinical literature suggests otherwise. The handful of documented cases of exceptionally complete autobiographical memory describe lives in which the past intrudes continuously, where a date mentioned in conversation summons the whole of a particular afternoon, and where reconciliation after an argument is extremely difficult because the argument does not fade. Memory researchers now generally regard forgetting as an active process rather than a leak: the system is not failing to hold information, it is deciding, by criteria we understand only partly, what deserves to remain available. Something similar appears to operate at the level of institutions and societies. Archives that keep everything become unusable, and the labor of a good archivist is largely the labor of destruction. Legal systems have built forgetting into their structure through limitation periods, after which a claim can no longer be brought, not because the wrong stopped mattering but because a society that permits any grievance to be revived indefinitely cannot settle anything. The arrival of technologies that do not forget has therefore changed something more fundamental than privacy. A remark made at nineteen remains available at forty, and the social mechanism that once allowed people to become different from their earlier selves — not forgiveness, which is rare, but ordinary forgetting, which was universal — has quietly been switched off. The consequences are easiest to see in the young, who are conducting their experiments in public and will be asked about them for the rest of their lives, but they extend further. A society in which nothing is allowed to recede is a society in which reputations become fixed early, and in which the incentive to change is weakened precisely where it matters most: among people whose earlier selves were worth abandoning.

questions.q: Why does the assumption about forgetting survive?
options: The costs of remembering are invisible
questions.note: İkinci cümle.

questions.q: What do documented cases of complete memory describe?
questions.note: Geçmiş sürekli araya giriyor.

questions.q: How do researchers now regard forgetting?
questions.note: "An active process rather than a leak."

questions.note: "Largely the labor of destruction."

questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Uzmanlığın sınırları
text: There is a category of question on which expert judgment reliably outperforms the amateur, and a second category on which it does not, and the two are frequently confused by experts and critics alike. Where a field offers rapid, unambiguous feedback, practice produces genuine skill. A surgeon learns within hours whether an operation succeeded; a chess player learns within minutes whether a move was sound. In such environments experience accumulates into judgment that can be trusted precisely because the world has been correcting it continuously. Now consider a field in which the feedback arrives years later, arrives mixed with a hundred other influences, and can be interpreted in several ways. Long-range political forecasting has this shape, as does the selection of employees and the prediction of which novel will sell. Studies of these domains report a disquieting result: experienced practitioners perform barely better than simple statistical rules, and sometimes worse, while remaining considerably more confident than either. The confidence is not fraudulent. It is produced by the same mechanism as genuine expertise — the accumulation of vivid, memorable cases — but without the corrective that would make the accumulation informative. What follows is not that expertise is worthless, which is the conclusion popular writing usually draws, but that the value of an expert depends on a property of the field rather than a property of the person. Before deferring to a specialist it is worth asking a single question: how quickly, and how unambiguously, does this person find out when they are wrong? The answer predicts more than any qualification. The practical difficulty is that fields with poor feedback tend to develop the strongest professional cultures, precisely because nothing external is available to settle disputes and status must therefore be conferred internally. Where the world corrects you, credentials matter less; where it does not, they become the only currency. This is why demands for humility, addressed to individuals, rarely change anything. The individual is responding rationally to the incentives of a field in which confidence is rewarded and error is never clearly assigned.

questions.q: In which fields does expertise reliably develop?
options: Where feedback is rapid and unambiguous
questions.note: "Where a field offers rapid, unambiguous feedback."

questions.q: What shape does long-range forecasting have?
options: Feedback arrives years later and mixed
questions.note: Geri bildirim yıllar sonra, yüz türlü etkiyle karışık geliyor.

questions.q: What do studies of such domains find?
options: Experts barely beat simple rules but are more confident
questions.note: "Barely better than simple statistical rules ... considerably more confident."

questions.q: How is the confidence produced?
options: By vivid memorable cases without correction
questions.note: Gerçek uzmanlıkla aynı mekanizma, ama düzeltici yok.

questions.q: What conclusion does the author reject?
questions.note: "Not that expertise is worthless, which is the conclusion popular writing usually draws."

questions.q: What single question should you ask?
options: How quickly does this person learn they are wrong?
questions.note: Son iki cümle.

title: Sokak adlarının siyaseti
text: A street name is the most widely distributed piece of official language in any city. It appears on documents, in conversation, on the envelopes of people who have no interest in history, and it does its work without ever being read as a statement. This is precisely what makes renaming so contentious. Those who defend an existing name usually argue that it is merely a label, emptied of meaning by daily use, and there is something to this: few residents of a street named after a general think about the general. Those who want the name changed reply that the emptiness is the point, since a commemoration nobody notices is the most durable kind. Both positions are stronger than their opponents allow. The practical consequences of renaming are real and are borne unequally. A shopkeeper reprints signs and stationery and loses customers who cannot find the address; a resident updates records with a dozen institutions, each of which has its own procedure. Cities that have handled the process well tend to share two features. They fund the administrative cost rather than transferring it to whoever happens to live there, and they treat the old name as information rather than as an embarrassment, leaving it visible on a small plate beneath the new one. The second measure irritates both camps, which is a reasonable indication that it is close to right: it denies the honor while preserving the fact, and it leaves a city whose surfaces record that an argument took place rather than one that appears always to have agreed with itself. There is a version of this argument that goes too far, and it is worth marking. If every contested name were retained beneath its replacement, the result would be a city as cluttered as a footnote, and the practice would lose its force through repetition. The measure works because it is exceptional, applied where the original decision was itself a public act rather than an accident of habit. Most streets are named after trees.

questions.q: Why is a street name unusual as official language?
options: It works without being read as a statement
questions.note: İlk iki cümle.

questions.q: What do defenders of an existing name argue?
options: It is merely a label emptied by use
questions.note: "It is merely a label, emptied of meaning by daily use."

questions.note: İşaretleri yeniden bastıran esnaf, kayıtlarını güncelleyen sakin.

options: Fund the cost and keep the old name visible

questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Çeviri makinesi ve anlam
text: Machine translation reached a standard two decades ago that its early designers had regarded as distant, and it did so by abandoning the assumption on which the field was founded. The original programs attempted to understand a sentence: to parse its structure, identify its parts, resolve its ambiguities and then reconstruct the meaning in another language. Progress was painfully slow. The systems that replaced them make no attempt to understand anything. They observe that certain sequences of words in one language have historically appeared alongside certain sequences in another, and they produce the sequence that the pattern makes most probable. By any reasonable measure the output is better. This ought to raise a question that the industry has mostly avoided: what does it tell us that a process with no comprehension whatever can produce text that competent speakers accept? One tempting answer is that understanding was never necessary, that meaning is exhausted by patterns of use, and that the machine has quietly settled a philosophical dispute in favor of one side. A second answer, harder to dismiss than it first appears, is that the machine is parasitic on understanding rather than independent of it. Every sentence in its training data was written by somebody who meant something, and the statistical shadow of all that meaning is what the system rearranges. On this view the translations are competent for the same reason that a well-made copy is accurate, and the moment the system is asked about a situation for which no human ever wrote a sentence, the limits of the arrangement become visible immediately. Neither answer can be settled by pointing at the output, which is what both camps keep doing. A translation that reads well is consistent with the machine having learned meaning and equally consistent with its having learned the shadow of meaning, and no amount of additional fluency distinguishes the two. What would distinguish them is performance in territory the training data never covered, which is precisely the territory where deployment is least common and evaluation least rigorous.

questions.q: What did the early programs attempt?
questions.note: "The original programs attempted to understand a sentence."

questions.q: What do the replacement systems do?
questions.note: "They produce the sequence that the pattern makes most probable."

questions.q: What question has the industry avoided?
options: What it means that a process without comprehension succeeds
questions.note: "What does it tell us that a process with no comprehension whatever can produce text..."

questions.q: What is the first tempting answer?
options: Meaning is exhausted by patterns of use
questions.note: İlk cevap: anlam kullanım örüntüleriyle tükeniyor.

questions.q: What does the second answer claim?
options: The machine is parasitic on human understanding
questions.note: "The machine is parasitic on understanding rather than independent of it."

options: When no human ever wrote about the situation
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Emeklilik yaşının aritmetiği
text: Governments that raise the retirement age generally present the decision as arithmetic rather than choice. People live longer, the ratio of workers to pensioners has fallen, and the sums no longer balance; the conclusion is said to follow. The premises are accurate and the conclusion does not follow, because arithmetic can only tell you that something must change, never which thing. A pension gap can be closed by later retirement, by higher contributions, by lower payments, by taxing other activities, or by raising the number of contributors through migration or employment policy. Each option distributes the cost to a different group, and presenting one of them as a mathematical necessity is a way of removing that distribution from discussion. The choice of later retirement has a further feature that is rarely stated in the announcements. Life expectancy has risen unevenly. In several countries the gap in healthy years between the richest and poorest groups exceeds a decade, and it is concentrated in exactly the occupations where the work is physical. A uniform increase in the retirement age therefore takes a larger proportion of remaining healthy life from a construction worker than from an accountant, while being presented as an equal measure because the number is the same. Some systems have responded with differentiated ages tied to occupation or to years of contribution rather than to birth date, which is administratively awkward and closer to the underlying reality. The awkwardness is often cited as a reason to prefer the uniform rule, an argument that mistakes the convenience of the administrator for a principle of fairness. It is also worth noticing what the framing does to the people affected. A worker told that the change is arithmetic has been told, in effect, that there is nobody to argue with. A worker told that the state has chosen one of five available options can ask why that one, and can be answered. The second conversation is harder to manage and is the only one that treats the listener as a citizen rather than as a variable.

questions.q: How is the decision usually presented?
questions.note: İlk cümle.

questions.q: What can arithmetic tell you?
options: That something must change, not which thing
questions.note: "Arithmetic can only tell you that something must change, never which thing."

options: It removes the distribution of cost from discussion
questions.note: Maliyetin kime yükleneceği tartışma dışına çıkıyor.

options: It has risen unevenly between groups
questions.note: "Life expectancy has risen unevenly."

questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Sıkılmanın kaybı
text: Boredom has almost disappeared from ordinary life, and the disappearance has been so convenient that its significance is easy to miss. Every interval that was previously empty — a line, a train journey, the minutes before sleep — can now be filled at no cost and with no planning. Since nobody enjoys being bored, the change looks like an unambiguous improvement, and for the shorter intervals it probably is. The complication concerns what boredom was doing. Psychologists who study the state describe it as an aversive signal, unpleasant by design, whose function is to push a person away from the current situation and towards something else. Whether that something else is productive is not determined in advance: a bored adolescent may write a novel or may break a window. What the signal guarantees is motion. Remove the discomfort and the motion becomes optional, which is why the most commonly reported consequence is not a decline in creative work but a curious flatness, a sense of days passing without any of them pressing hard enough to force a change. There is a second effect, less often discussed. Boredom is where a person encounters their own company without a task, and that encounter, though frequently unpleasant, is the standard route to noticing what one actually thinks. A life in which the interval never arrives is a life in which that noticing is always postponed. None of this argues for manufacturing boredom deliberately, which would be as artificial as avoiding it. It argues for leaving one or two intervals unfilled, and for treating the restlessness that follows not as a problem to be solved but as information about what has been missing. The claim is modest and should be kept modest, because the literature is thinner than the confident essays on the subject suggest, and because the interval that suits one person is unbearable to another. What can be said with reasonable confidence is that the removal happened without anybody choosing it, as a side effect of a device becoming small enough to carry, and that changes which nobody decided are the ones most worth examining afterwards.

questions.q: Why is the disappearance of boredom easy to miss?
questions.note: İlk cümle.

questions.q: How do psychologists describe boredom?
options: An aversive signal, unpleasant by design
questions.note: "An aversive signal, unpleasant by design."

questions.note: "What the signal guarantees is motion."

questions.q: What is the most commonly reported consequence?
questions.note: "Not a decline in creative work but a curious flatness."

questions.q: What is the second effect?
options: Noticing what one thinks is always postponed
questions.note: Kendi şirketiyle görevsiz karşılaşma ertelenir.

questions.q: What does the author finally argue for?
options: Leaving one or two intervals unfilled
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Anonimliğin iki yüzü
titleEn: The Case For and Against Anonymity
text: The argument that anonymity degrades public conversation has an obvious empirical basis and a less obvious weakness. The basis is that people say things under a false name they would not say under their own, and anybody who has read a comment section understands the point without further evidence. The weakness is that the same property is what allows a nurse to describe conditions on a ward, a citizen of an unfriendly state to report what is happening in it, and a person with a diagnosis to ask a question they could not ask in their own town. Proposals to require real names therefore trade one harm for another, and the trade is usually presented as though only one side of it existed. It is also worth noticing what the proposals would not achieve. Studies of platforms that require verified identity find that abuse falls but does not disappear, and that the abuse which remains is disproportionately committed by people who are entirely comfortable being identified, because their community approves. The mechanism that restrains most people is not the fear of exposure but the presence of an audience whose opinion they value, and a real-name policy does nothing about a person whose audience shares their view. What has worked better, where it has been tried, is stranger and less satisfying: not identifying the speaker but slowing the speech. Platforms that impose a delay between writing and publishing, or that require a comment to be read once before it can be posted, report reductions comparable to identity requirements and without the cost to the nurse. The finding is unwelcome to both camps in the argument, which is usually a sign that it is measuring something real. It suggests that most of what we call cruelty online is not a settled disposition but a momentary one, and that the design question is not who is speaking but how quickly they were allowed to.

questions.q: What is the weakness of the anti-anonymity argument?
options: The same property protects people who need it
questions.note: "The same property is what allows a nurse to describe conditions on a ward."

questions.q: What do studies of verified platforms find?
options: Abuse falls but does not disappear
questions.note: "Abuse falls but does not disappear."

questions.q: Who commits the remaining abuse?
questions.note: "Disproportionately committed by people who are entirely comfortable being identified."

questions.q: What actually restrains most people?
options: An audience whose opinion they value
questions.note: "The presence of an audience whose opinion they value."

questions.q: What has worked better?
options: Slowing the speech rather than identifying the speaker
questions.note: "Not identifying the speaker but slowing the speech."

title: Ölçülemeyen işin değeri
titleEn: The Work That Leaves No Trace
text: Certain kinds of labor are recognized only by their absence. A building that does not catch fire, a system that is not attacked, a conflict that does not escalate: in each case the outcome is nothing happening, and the people responsible for that nothing occupy an awkward position in any organization that measures output. Their success produces no artifact. Worse, sustained success actively undermines the case for continuing to fund them, since a decade without incident is readily interpreted as evidence that the risk was overstated in the first place. The pattern is so reliable that it can be stated as a rule: preventive work is cut in proportion to how well it has been performed. What makes this more than an administrative curiosity is that the people doing the work understand the dynamic perfectly well, and it shapes their conduct in ways that are rarely acknowledged. A safety team that is never visible has no constituency when the budget is reviewed, so competent teams learn to generate visible activity — reports, exercises, briefings — whose primary function is to demonstrate existence rather than to reduce risk. This is not dishonesty. It is the rational response to an environment that will not otherwise notice them, and the cost is that some proportion of the available effort is diverted from the work into the documentation of the work. The organizations that have escaped this trap are few and share an unusual feature. They have made the counterfactual explicit, requiring the preventive function to state in advance what it expects to prevent and at what rate, so that a quiet year can be recognized as a result rather than mistaken for an absence of need. It is a clumsy instrument and it fails in both directions. It remains the only serious attempt anybody has made to pay for something that, when it works, looks exactly like nothing at all.

questions.q: How is this kind of work recognized?
questions.note: "Certain kinds of labor are recognized only by their absence."

questions.q: What does sustained success do?
options: Undermines the case for funding the work
questions.note: "Sustained success actively undermines the case for continuing to fund them."

questions.q: Why do competent teams generate visible activity?
options: To demonstrate existence in a system that would not notice them
questions.note: "Whose primary function is to demonstrate existence rather than to reduce risk."

questions.q: What is the cost of that response?
options: Effort moves from the work to documenting it
questions.note: "Some proportion of the available effort is diverted from the work into the documentation."

questions.q: What do the few successful organizations do?
options: Make the counterfactual explicit in advance
questions.note: "They have made the counterfactual explicit."

title: Yasanın geriye yürümesi
titleEn: Judging the Past by Present Rules
text: There is a principle, close to universal in developed legal systems, that a person may not be punished under a law that did not exist when they acted. Its justification is not sentimental. A rule that can be written afterwards is not a rule at all but an instrument, and a citizen who cannot know in advance what is forbidden cannot meaningfully choose to obey. The principle nonetheless produces outcomes that are difficult to accept, and the difficulty is not resolved by restating the principle more firmly. Consider a practice that was lawful, widely known, and is now understood to have caused serious harm. The people responsible cannot be prosecuted, and the argument that they should be is not stupid: they knew what they were doing, the harm was foreseeable to anybody who looked, and the lawfulness of the practice was itself the product of their influence over the people writing the law. What the principle protects, in such a case, is precisely the person least deserving of protection. Legal systems have developed partial answers, none of them satisfying. Civil liability, which operates on a different standard and can reach conduct that was not criminal. Public inquiries, which establish a record without imposing a penalty and are routinely dismissed as inadequate by the people they are meant to satisfy. Disqualification from future office, which is preventive rather than punitive and attracts the objection that it is punishment under another name. The honest account is that the principle costs something and is worth its cost, and that the cost falls unevenly on people who have no say in the matter. Systems that pretend otherwise, by quietly stretching definitions until an old act becomes a current offence, buy a single satisfying outcome at the price of the thing that made the system worth defending.

questions.q: What is the justification for the principle?
options: A citizen must be able to know in advance what is forbidden
questions.note: "A citizen who cannot know in advance what is forbidden cannot meaningfully choose to obey."

questions.q: Why is the opposing argument not stupid?
options: The harm was foreseeable and the law reflected their influence
questions.note: "The lawfulness of the practice was itself the product of their influence."

questions.q: What does the principle protect in such cases?
options: The person least deserving of protection
questions.note: "What the principle protects... is precisely the person least deserving of protection."

questions.q: What objection is raised against disqualification?
options: That it is punishment under another name
questions.note: "Attracts the objection that it is punishment under another name."

questions.q: What is the writer's honest account?
options: The principle costs something and is worth its cost
questions.note: "The principle costs something and is worth its cost."

title: Yaşlanan nüfusun sessiz hesabı
text: Of all the large problems facing wealthy states, demographic ageing is the one about which there is least genuine disagreement and least useful action, and the two facts are connected. The arithmetic is not contested by anybody: a population in which the ratio of working-age people to retired people falls steadily will, absent some other change, find that the promises made to the second group cannot be met from the contributions of the first. Every serious participant accepts this. What is disputed is which of four unpopular adjustments to make, and since each has a clearly identifiable group of losers who exist now, while the beneficiaries are diffuse and largely in the future, the stable political equilibrium is to describe the problem accurately and postpone. The four adjustments are familiar. Raise the retirement age, which falls hardest on manual workers whose bodies are the reason the age was set where it was. Raise contributions, which reduces the income of people currently working. Reduce payments, which breaks a promise that people arranged their lives around. Increase the number of contributors through immigration, which is the only option that expands rather than divides the total, and the one that has proved least available politically in most of the countries that need it most. What is genuinely unusual about the debate is the relationship between knowledge and action. This is not a case of disputed science, competing models or hidden data. The projections have been published, repeatedly, for forty years, and have proved conservative. A political system that cannot act on a forecast this uncontested is not suffering from insufficient information, and the persistent proposal to commission further study is best understood not as a request for evidence but as a way of agreeing that something must be done at some point by somebody else.

questions.q: Why is there little useful action?
options: The losers exist now and the gainers are in the future
questions.note: "Each has a clearly identifiable group of losers who exist now, while the beneficiaries are diffuse."

questions.q: Why does raising the retirement age fall hardest on manual workers?
options: Their bodies are the reason the age was set there
questions.note: "Whose bodies are the reason the age was set where it was."

questions.q: Which option expands rather than divides the total?
questions.note: "Increase the number of contributors through immigration."

questions.q: What does the writer say about the projections?
options: Published for forty years and proved conservative
questions.note: "Published, repeatedly, for forty years, and have proved conservative."

questions.q: How does the writer read calls for further study?
options: As a way of leaving action to somebody else
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Kurgu odasının sessiz yazarlığı
text: A documentary that contains no false statement can still be substantially untrue, and the mechanism is not deception in any sense the maker would recognize. Two hundred hours of material become ninety minutes, and every decision in that reduction is an argument about what the material means. A subject who spoke for six hours appears for ninety seconds, and which ninety seconds is a judgment the viewer cannot inspect. Sequence performs the same work more quietly: two events placed adjacently acquire a causal relationship that neither the film nor the maker has asserted and that the viewer supplies without noticing. Music is the least defensible of the instruments and the most used, since it instructs the audience how to feel about a face before the face has said anything. None of this is avoidable. A film without selection is not a film, and the demand that documentary be neutral rests on a confusion about what a camera does. The honest position is therefore not neutrality but disclosure, and the forms it can take are more varied than is usually recognized. A maker can show the question as well as the answer. A maker can leave in the moment where a subject asks to stop. A maker can decline to use music under an interview, which is a decision the audience will not register consciously and which changes what they are able to think. What distinguishes the documentaries that survive is rarely their subject and almost always this: the viewer finishes with a clear sense of having been shown an argument, rather than a clear sense of having seen what happened. Makers who achieve the second effect are usually praised for it, which is a fair description of the problem. The reviewer who writes that a film simply lets the facts speak has paid the maker the highest available compliment and identified, without meaning to, the exact point at which the audience stopped being able to argue back. Facts do not speak. Somebody chose the order, and the better that choice was, the less visible it is.

questions.q: How can a documentary be untrue without false statements?
options: Through the decisions made in reducing the material
questions.note: "Every decision in that reduction is an argument about what the material means."

questions.q: What does sequence do?
options: Creates a causal relationship the viewer supplies
questions.note: "Two events placed adjacently acquire a causal relationship."

questions.q: Why is music the least defensible instrument?
options: It instructs the audience how to feel before anything is said
questions.note: "It instructs the audience how to feel about a face before the face has said anything."

questions.q: What is the honest position?
questions.note: "The honest position is therefore not neutrality but disclosure."

questions.q: What distinguishes documentaries that survive?
options: The viewer knows they were shown an argument
questions.note: "The viewer finishes with a clear sense of having been shown an argument."

title: Uzmana danışmanın maliyeti
text: A person facing a decision outside their competence is advised to consult an expert, and the advice is sound as far as it goes. What it omits is that the question being asked and the question the expert is equipped to answer are frequently not the same, and that neither party is well placed to notice the gap. A surgeon asked whether an operation is possible will answer a question about surgery. The question the patient meant was whether the remaining years would be better with the operation or without it, and that question contains a great deal that the surgeon has no special access to: what the patient can tolerate, what they want their remaining time to contain, how much they fear one kind of decline relative to another. The surgeon is not overreaching by answering; they have answered exactly what was asked. The failure occurred at the point of translation, and it is invisible because both sides believe the conversation went well. This has a practical consequence that runs against the usual advice about seeking second opinions. A second expert in the same discipline will very often confirm the first, not because the first was right about the patient's life but because both are answering the technical question correctly. The useful second opinion is frequently from a different discipline entirely, or from somebody who has made the same decision and lived with it. Professions differ markedly in how well they handle this. Some have built the translation into the encounter, training practitioners to ask what the person is hoping the decision will achieve before describing what is technically available. Others treat such questions as outside their remit, which is defensible as a description of their training and leaves the most consequential part of the decision to whoever happens to be in the room.

questions.q: What does the usual advice omit?
options: The question asked and the one answered may differ
questions.note: "The question being asked and the question the expert is equipped to answer are frequently not the same."

questions.q: What does the patient's real question contain?
options: Things the surgeon has no special access to
questions.note: "That question contains a great deal that the surgeon has no special access to."

questions.q: Why is the failure invisible?
options: Both sides believe the conversation went well
questions.note: "It is invisible because both sides believe the conversation went well."

questions.q: Why does a second opinion often confirm the first?
options: Both answer the technical question correctly
questions.note: "Both are answering the technical question correctly."

questions.q: What do the better professions do?
options: Ask what the person hopes the decision will achieve
questions.note: "Training practitioners to ask what the person is hoping the decision will achieve."

title: Kamusal alanın özelleşmesi
titleEn: The Square That Belongs to Somebody
text: A great deal of what appears to be public space in modern cities is privately owned, and the distinction is invisible until it becomes relevant. The paving is continuous, the benches are comfortable, the planting is better maintained than anything the city manages, and there is no sign at the boundary. What differs is the rule. A genuinely public square is governed by law, which is slow, contested and appealable. Its privately owned equivalent is governed by the conditions of entry, which can forbid photography, assembly, sleeping, skateboarding or remaining without making a purchase, and which can be changed by the owner without notice or explanation. Nothing about this is concealed; it is simply not announced, and almost nobody reads the conditions of entry to a paved area. Defenders of the arrangement make a reasonable point. Cities acquired these spaces at no cost to the public purse, and they are cleaner and safer than what preceded them, which was frequently a car park. The objection is not that the spaces are bad but that the transfer was not described. A city that sells the right to make rules in the center of itself has done something that a city which builds a square has not, and residents who experience the two as identical have not consented to the difference because they were never told there was one. The reform that has been tried in several places is modest and revealing in its reception. It requires nothing more than a sign at each entrance stating who owns the ground and listing what is forbidden. Owners have resisted this with a force entirely out of proportion to the cost of a sign, which tells you what the sign would cost them. The point is not that the rules are unreasonable. Most of them are the rules any careful landlord would write, and a city square governed by law also forbids a great deal. The point is that one set was arrived at through a process a resident can enter and the other was not, and the difference only becomes visible on the day somebody wants to stand in the square and say something the owner would rather not host.

questions.q: What makes the distinction invisible?
questions.note: "There is no sign at the boundary."

questions.q: How is a genuinely public square governed?
options: By law, which is contested and appealable
questions.note: "A genuinely public square is governed by law."

questions.q: What is the defenders' reasonable point?
options: The spaces cost the public nothing and replaced car parks
questions.note: "Cities acquired these spaces at no cost to the public purse."

questions.q: What is the writer's actual objection?
questions.note: "The objection is not that the spaces are bad but that the transfer was not described."

questions.q: What does resistance to the sign reveal?
options: What the sign would cost the owners
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Bilimsel makalenin biçimi
titleEn: The Paper That Hides Its Own History
text: The standard scientific paper describes a process that did not occur. It opens with a question, proceeds to a method chosen to answer it, reports what was found and concludes. The actual work almost never proceeded in that order. The question was frequently arrived at after the results were in, the method was partly determined by what equipment was free that month, and several lines of enquiry were abandoned without appearing anywhere in the published account. None of this is fraud. The convention exists because the reconstructed version is easier to evaluate: a reader wishing to know whether the conclusion follows from the evidence is not helped by a chronological account of eighteen months of confusion. The cost is that the form conceals precisely the information needed to judge how much the result should be believed. A hypothesis formed before the data was collected and one formed after it have very different evidential weight, and the paper makes them typographically identical. The reforms that address this are recent and their adoption is uneven. Pre-registration, in which the question and the analysis are deposited publicly before the data exists, separates the two cases cleanly and has produced an instructive result: in fields where it has been adopted, the proportion of studies reporting the effect they set out to find has fallen sharply. This was predicted by its advocates and treated as an objection by its opponents, and both were describing the same number. What the convention protected was not dishonesty but a form of self-deception available to entirely honest people, which is harder to argue against and considerably more common. The objection most often raised is that pre-registration suits some fields and not others, and this is correct. Work that sets out to find what is there rather than to test a stated expectation cannot be registered in advance without destroying the thing that makes it valuable. The answer is not to exempt such work but to label it, so that a reader knows which kind of claim is being made before deciding how much weight to give it.

questions.q: What does the standard paper describe?
options: The exact order of the work
A process that did not occur
questions.note: "The standard scientific paper describes a process that did not occur."

questions.q: Why does the convention exist?
options: The reconstructed version is easier to evaluate
questions.note: "Because the reconstructed version is easier to evaluate."

questions.q: What is the cost of the form?
options: It conceals what is needed to judge the result
questions.note: "The form conceals precisely the information needed to judge how much the result should be believed."

questions.q: What does pre-registration separate?
options: Hypotheses formed before and after the data
questions.note: "Separates the two cases cleanly."

questions.q: What was the convention protecting?
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Sadeliğin pahalılığı
text: A product with three buttons is frequently more expensive to develop than one with thirty, and the reason is not materials. Every feature that does not appear in the finished object represents a decision that somebody had to make and then defend, and the defense is structurally harder than the alternative. A feature that is included can be justified by the person who wanted it; a feature that is excluded must be refused by somebody willing to say no to a colleague who has a reason. Multiply this across four hundred proposals and the organizations that produce simple objects are not the ones with better taste but the ones that have arranged for refusal to be somebody's job. There is a further cost that is easier to overlook. Removing a control does not remove the underlying decision it represented; it relocates the decision into the object, which must now make it automatically and correctly in circumstances its designers did not foresee. A device with a manual setting fails visibly and is adjusted by its owner. A device that decides for itself fails invisibly and is described by its owner as being broken for no reason. Simplicity of this kind therefore transfers work from the user to the engineer, and the transfer is only worthwhile where the engineer genuinely knows more about the situation than the person holding the object, which is a narrower set of cases than the industry's enthusiasm suggests. The products that age well tend to be those that removed the controls nobody used and kept the one that everybody eventually needs, and identifying which is which requires the kind of long observation that almost nobody funds. The information exists, in the sense that every repair shop and every support line knows exactly which control the customer is calling about. It is simply held at the point furthest from the people making the decision, and by an organization that classifies it as a cost rather than as the only honest account of how the object is actually used.

questions.q: Why is a simple product expensive to develop?
options: Every excluded feature had to be refused by somebody
questions.note: "A feature that is excluded must be refused by somebody willing to say no."

questions.q: What distinguishes organizations that make simple objects?
questions.note: "The ones that have arranged for refusal to be somebody's job."

questions.q: What does removing a control do?
options: Relocates the decision into the object
questions.note: "It relocates the decision into the object."

questions.q: How does an automatic device fail?
options: Invisibly, and seems broken for no reason
questions.note: "A device that decides for itself fails invisibly."

questions.q: When is the transfer worthwhile?
options: When the engineer genuinely knows more than the user
questions.note: "Only worthwhile where the engineer genuinely knows more about the situation."

title: Tanıklığın yazıya geçirilmesi
text: An oral account becomes a document through a series of small operations, each defensible and each subtractive. Hesitation is removed, since a transcript peppered with pauses is unreadable and the pauses were not the point. Repetition is condensed, on the reasonable ground that the speaker said the same thing three times. Grammar is corrected, out of respect, so that the speaker does not appear on the page less articulate than they were in the room. Digression is cut, because the account has to be about something. Every one of these decisions improves the document and removes evidence, and the evidence removed is disproportionately about the speaker's relationship to what they are describing. A person who hesitates before a date is telling you something about the date. A person who repeats a sentence three times is telling you which sentence matters. Archives that have understood this have moved, where resources allow, to keeping the recording as the record and treating the transcript as a finding aid rather than a substitute. The difficulty is that a recording is almost never consulted. A researcher with four hundred interviews and a deadline reads transcripts, and will continue to, and the honest response to that is not to demand better habits from researchers but to design the transcript so that its own limitations are legible: marking where material was cut, preserving hesitation at the points where it carries weight, and stating at the head of the document what conventions were applied. None of this recovers what was lost. It does tell the reader that something was. That is a smaller claim than the one usually made for good practice in this field, and it is the one that survives contact with a deadline. A reader who knows that a document is partial will read it differently, ask different questions of it, and go to the recording on the two occasions out of four hundred when the answer actually matters.

questions.q: What do the small operations have in common?
options: Each is defensible and each removes something
questions.note: "Each defensible and each subtractive."

questions.q: What does hesitation before a date indicate?
questions.note: "A person who hesitates before a date is telling you something about the date."

questions.q: What have some archives moved to?
options: Keeping the recording as the record
questions.note: "Keeping the recording as the record."

questions.q: What is the difficulty with recordings?
options: They cannot be searched at all
questions.note: "A recording is almost never consulted."

questions.q: What does the writer propose instead?
questions.note: "Design the transcript so that its own limitations are legible."

title: Kurumsal özrün anatomisi
text: An institutional apology can be read almost entirely from its grammar, and the reading is more reliable than any assessment of its sincerity. The decisive feature is who appears as the subject of the verb. Mistakes were made describes an event with no author; the passive has removed the one piece of information the sentence existed to supply. We are sorry that some people felt distressed relocates the harm into the perceptions of the injured party, and the word some quietly disputes the number. We apologize for any offense caused converts a specific act into a hypothetical one, since any is doing the work of admitting nothing in particular. These constructions are not accidents of style. They are produced by a process in which a legal department is asked to approve a text whose purpose is to accept responsibility, and the two aims are in direct conflict: an admission that satisfies the injured party is admissible in a court, and one that satisfies the lawyer does not satisfy anybody else. The organizations that have escaped this have generally done so by settling the legal question first and then writing the apology, which is expensive and looks from outside like the delay it is. What makes the subject worth examining is not the hypocrisy, which is ordinary, but the consistency. An apology's grammar predicts subsequent behavior better than its adjectives do. A statement naming an actor and an action is very often followed by a change in practice; a statement in which the harm happens by itself is very rarely followed by anything at all, and the people who received it usually knew that within a day of reading it. This is not a difficult test to apply and it requires no access to anybody's intentions. It can be run on a page of text in under a minute, which is a great deal more than can be said for most of what is written about corporate sincerity.

questions.q: What is the decisive feature of an apology?
options: Who appears as the subject of the verb
questions.note: "The decisive feature is who appears as the subject of the verb."

questions.q: What does 'mistakes were made' remove?
questions.note: "The passive has removed the one piece of information the sentence existed to supply."

questions.q: Why are these constructions produced?
options: A legal department approves a text meant to accept responsibility
questions.note: "A legal department is asked to approve a text whose purpose is to accept responsibility."

questions.q: How have some organizations escaped it?
options: By settling the legal question first
questions.note: "Settling the legal question first and then writing the apology."

questions.q: What does the grammar predict?
options: Whether a change in practice will follow
questions.note: "An apology's grammar predicts subsequent behavior better than its adjectives do."

title: Sanatta özgünlük sorusu
titleEn: The Value of Knowing Who Made It
text: When a painting long attributed to a major figure is reassigned to a workshop assistant, its price collapses and its appearance does not change by a single brushstroke. The usual response to this is amused contempt for a market that has confused an object with a signature. The contempt is too quick. Some of the value that disappears is indeed speculative, but a considerable part of it is informational, and the information is genuinely lost. A work by a known artist sits inside an account of a life: it can be dated, placed among other works, read as a development of something earlier or a retreat from it. Reassigned to an unnamed assistant, the same canvas becomes an object about which almost nothing further can be said, and the loss is real even for a viewer who has never thought about money. There is a second consideration that complicates the picture further. A great deal of art made before the nineteenth century was produced by workshops in which the master's contribution might be a design, a face, or a supervisory glance, and the modern demand for a single author imposes a category that the objects themselves do not support. Museums have handled this with increasing honesty, replacing confident labels with descriptions of what is actually known. Auction houses have not, because the ambiguity has no price. The most interesting consequence is what happens to the demoted painting itself. A canvas that hung for eighty years as a minor work by a major figure is frequently seen for the first time, by curators and visitors alike, on the day it stops being one. Until then it was read through the name, and everything in it that did not fit the name was either not noticed or quietly explained as a weak passage. Removed from that account, the picture has to be looked at, and a surprising number of such works turn out to reward the attention, which is an argument for the reassignment that almost nobody making it bothers to use.

questions.q: What does not change when a work is reassigned?
questions.note: "Its appearance does not change by a single brushstroke."

questions.q: What kind of value is genuinely lost?
questions.note: "A considerable part of it is informational, and the information is genuinely lost."

questions.q: What does a known artist's work sit inside?
questions.note: "A work by a known artist sits inside an account of a life."

questions.q: What does the modern demand for a single author do?
options: Imposes a category the objects do not support
questions.note: "Imposes a category that the objects themselves do not support."

questions.q: What happens to the demoted painting?
options: It is often really seen for the first time
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Alışkanlığın kırılma anı
titleEn: The Window That Opens When Life Changes
text: Behavior that has resisted every deliberate effort at change frequently alters by itself when a person moves house, starts a job or has a child. The finding is robust and its explanation is uncomfortable for anyone who believes that habits are primarily a matter of will. A habit is held in place not by the desire to perform it but by a stable set of cues: the same route, the same kitchen, the same people at the same hour. Remove the cues and the behavior loses its support, which is why a smoker who has failed eleven times may succeed in the month of a relocation without any additional resolve. The practical implication is that the moment matters more than the method, and that the moments are few, brief and unannounced. Public health programmes have begun to act on this, targeting the weeks around a move or a birth rather than January, with results that exceed anything achieved by conventional campaigns. The same mechanism has an unwelcome symmetry that the literature discusses less. Disruption removes the support for good habits too. A person who exercised reliably for six years may simply stop on changing job, not through any decision but because the route home no longer passes the pool, and will often describe the change as a loss of motivation, which is an explanation that locates in the character something that happened in the street. Anybody planning a large change would do better to spend an hour asking which of their current habits are being held up by the arrangement they are about to dismantle. The exercise is short and almost nobody performs it, because the behaviors in question are invisible precisely to the degree that they are working. A person can list every intention they have failed to keep and will rarely think to list the walk they have taken four times a week for six years without once deciding to.

questions.q: What holds a habit in place?
questions.note: "A habit is held in place not by the desire to perform it but by a stable set of cues."

questions.q: Why might a smoker succeed during a move?
questions.note: "Remove the cues and the behavior loses its support."

questions.q: What are public health programs now targeting?
options: The weeks around a move or a birth
questions.note: "Targeting the weeks around a move or a birth rather than January."

questions.q: What is the unwelcome symmetry?
options: Disruption removes support for good habits too
questions.note: "Disruption removes the support for good habits too."

questions.q: What does the writer recommend before a large change?
options: Ask which behaviors depend on the current arrangement
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Yardımın koşulları
text: Aid given with conditions attached has an obvious justification and a less obvious record. The justification is that money handed over without requirements may be spent badly, and there is no shortage of cases in which it was. The record is that the conditions themselves consume a substantial fraction of the value transferred. A grant requiring quarterly reporting in a specified format obliges the receiving body to employ somebody to produce those reports, and where the receiving body is a clinic with fourteen staff the post is filled by taking a person away from the work the grant was meant to support. Where several donors each impose their own format, the administrative load can exceed the marginal benefit of the later grants entirely, a threshold that is crossed silently and is visible only to the people filling in the forms. The research on unconditional transfers is now substantial and its findings are consistently uncomfortable for the sector. Money handed directly to households, with no instruction about its use, is spent on much what an economist would predict and much what the recipients would say if asked: school fees, a roof, a stock of goods to sell. The predicted waste is measurable and small. This has not produced the change in practice that the evidence would justify, and the reason is worth stating plainly. A donor who transfers money without conditions has also transferred the decision, and with it the ability to describe what the money achieved. The conditions were never only about the risk of waste. They were about retaining the authorship of the outcome, which is a legitimate thing for a donor to want and a poor reason to make a clinic hire an administrator. There is a middle position that some funders have reached and that is rarely described, perhaps because it sounds like a retreat. They attach no conditions to the spending and heavy conditions to the reporting of outcomes, which leaves the decision where it belongs and keeps the donor able to say what happened. It costs the recipient a form at the end rather than a post for the duration.

questions.q: What do the conditions consume?
options: A substantial fraction of the value transferred
questions.note: "The conditions themselves consume a substantial fraction of the value transferred."

questions.q: What happens in a clinic with fourteen staff?
options: Somebody is taken away from the work to file reports
questions.note: "The post is filled by taking a person away from the work the grant was meant to support."

questions.q: What can happen when several donors impose formats?
options: The load exceeds the benefit of later grants
questions.note: "The administrative load can exceed the marginal benefit of the later grants."

questions.q: What does research on unconditional transfers find?
questions.note: "The predicted waste is measurable and small."

questions.q: What were the conditions really about?
questions.note: "They were about retaining the authorship of the outcome."

title: Bilginin tarihi
titleEn: The Footnote and What It Promises
text: The footnote is a small and strange invention whose function is frequently misunderstood. It is generally taken to be a device for giving credit, and it does that, but its older and more important purpose is to make a claim checkable by a stranger. A sentence with a reference attached says something the sentence alone cannot: that the author is prepared to be found wrong by anybody willing to walk to a library. This is a considerable commitment and it explains a pattern that otherwise looks merely pedantic. Disciplines with dense referencing are not more honest than those without; they are differently exposed, and the exposure disciplines the writing in ways that survive even where nobody checks. The habit has weakened for reasons that have nothing to do with intellectual decline. A link rots. A reference to a database that has been reorganized points at nothing, and a claim supported by a source the reader cannot reach is functionally an assertion. Archival projects address part of this and are chronically underfunded, since preserving the ability to check a claim made in 2009 has no constituency and produces nothing anybody can announce. What has largely disappeared, and is worth naming because its loss is invisible, is the negative footnote: the note that says a plausible alternative was considered and rejected, and why. It costs an author something to write, since it names a possibility the reader might not otherwise have thought of and invites them to weigh it. Its absence is not detectable by any reader, which is precisely what makes its presence informative about the person who wrote it. An author who includes such notes is telling a reader that the argument was contested in private before it was published, and that the version on the page survived the contest. No formal system can require this, and any attempt to require it would produce a hundred thousand notes rejecting alternatives nobody seriously held.

questions.q: What is the footnote's older purpose?
options: To make a claim checkable by a stranger
questions.note: "Its older and more important purpose is to make a claim checkable by a stranger."

questions.q: What does a reference commit the author to?
options: Being found wrong by anybody who looks
questions.note: "The author is prepared to be found wrong by anybody willing to walk to a library."

questions.q: How does the writer describe densely referenced fields?
questions.note: "They are differently exposed."

questions.q: What has weakened the habit?
options: Links and databases that no longer resolve
